label: Laptop

questions.text: How many hours a day is the laptop used?
questions.why: Long daily use wears the battery, fans and keyboard.
Soft surfaces block the air vents and trap heat.
Poor or mismatched chargers are a common cause of battery and port damage.
A backup protects your work if a repair or drive fails.

questions.text: Do you eat or drink near the laptop?
questions.why: Spills are a common cause of keyboard and board damage.

questions.text: Have you noticed loud fans, overheating, a swollen battery or a slow start?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Stop using the laptop and keep it away from anything that can burn if the battery swells, gets very hot or smells unusual.
care_tips.why: A damaged battery can catch fire.

care_tips.text: Don't open, puncture or crush the battery, and don't use it after a hard fall that dented it.
care_tips.why: Damaged battery cells can overheat or catch fire.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the laptop before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: Cleaning an appliance that is plugged in risks an electric shock.

care_tips.text: Use the laptop on a hard, flat surface so the vents are not blocked.
Use the laptop's own charger or one with the same rating from the brand.
care_tips.why: A wrong charger can damage the battery and the charging circuit.
A repair or a failed drive can lose your data.

care_tips.text: Keep drinks away from the keyboard.
care_tips.why: Spills damage the keyboard and the board inside.

care_tips.text: Carry the laptop in a padded bag.
If it overheats, the fans get loud or it slows down a lot, contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: These can be signs of a cooling or drive problem.

reminders.text: Back up the files on your laptop.
reminders.note: Check your manual or system settings for automatic backup.

reminders.text: Check the laptop's vents are free of dust (switched off and unplugged).
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
